projects.againBody: The progress of every part is cleared and you start with the first part. The patterns stay as they are. This can’t be undone.
projects.title: Your projects

empty.title: Start your first project
empty.body: A project is what you knit, e.g. a sweater. It is made of patterns (e.g. body, sleeve), and each pattern of charts. Everything stays on this device.

projects.deleteBody: The project, its patterns and progress will be removed from this device. To keep them, save the project to a file first.

newProject.name: Project name
newProject.fromPdf: Upload a PDF with the pattern description
newProject.fromPdfHint: We recognise the charts, the legend and the order of charts in a round. Then we check it together.
newProject.createHint: Choose what you knit. You add the patterns and charts yourself.
newProject.notPdf: This is not a PDF file.
newProject.limits: PDF up to {{mb}} MB and {{pages}} pages.
newProject.privacy: The file is read only on this device. Nothing is sent.
newProject.title: New project

settings.title: Settings
settings.wakeLock: Keep the screen on while knitting
settings.wakeLockHint: Works while a project is open. Some browsers don't support it.
settings.storageMemory: This browser doesn't allow saving data. Progress will be lost when the page closes.
settings.storagePersisted: Data is saved on this device and the browser won't remove it on its own.
settings.storageBestEffort: Data is saved on this device. The browser may remove it when space runs low – keep backups.
settings.privacy: Projects and progress never leave the device. The app has no account and no analytics.
settings.restoreHint: Adds the projects from the backup. Nothing newer on this device is overwritten.
settings.restoreRule: New ones and newer ones in the backup are written with their progress. Newer ones on this device stay as they are.
settings.restoreSkipped_one: {{count}} damaged entry in the file skipped.
settings.restoreSkipped_other: {{count}} damaged entries in the file skipped.

sync.local-only: Sync: this device only. To move projects to another device, save a backup and restore it there.

memory.title: Progress won't be saved.
memory.body: The browser blocks saving data (for example in private mode). Open the app in a normal window.

update.available: A new version of the app is ready.

notFound.title: Page not found
notFound.body: This address doesn't lead to any screen.

error.pattern-missing: This pattern is not in the project
error.no-patterns: This project has no pattern yet

tracker.saveFailed: The last change couldn't be saved. It will be retried with the next one.

status.label: Current position
status.nothingYet: Nothing done yet. Tap a stitch to mark it and every stitch before it.
status.counterRows_one: {{count}} row done. Tap “{{button}}” after each row.
status.counterRows_other: {{count}} rows done. Tap “{{button}}” after each row.
status.counterRounds_one: {{count}} round done. Tap “{{button}}” after each round.
status.counterRounds_other: {{count}} rounds done. Tap “{{button}}” after each round.

grid.label: Chart grid
grid.help: Tap a stitch to mark it. Drag to move, pinch to zoom. Keyboard: arrow keys move the cursor, Enter marks the stitch under it.
grid.unsupported: This browser can’t draw the grid. Try a current version of Safari, Chrome or Firefox.

view.title: View
view.veil: Dim rows above the current one
view.rowsEnd: To the end of the pattern

actions.doneHint: Finish this part and go on to the next one
actions.label: Actions
actions.eraserHint: Eraser: tap a done stitch to go back to it (E)

editor.saveError: Not saved – check the fields marked in red
editor.notesHint: Your notes, e.g. needles, yarn, gauge. They stay on this device.
editor.sizesHint: Stitch and row counts in patterns can differ per size.
editor.noCharts: The pattern has no charts yet. Add the first one, e.g. a cable or ribbing.
editor.legendHint: Enter each symbol's number and description as in your pattern. They're shown next to the grid while knitting.
editor.legendEmpty: Symbols show up here once you draw a chart.
editor.fixFirst: Fix the errors to start knitting this pattern.
editor.hasGauge: The designer states a gauge (10 × 10 cm)
editor.gaugeHint: Used to estimate rows in “knit until X cm” patterns. You set your own gauge while knitting, in the project settings.
editor.continueStageHint: A new pattern right after this one, with the same charts and layout. The charts continue from the next row and you change the layout (decreases, increases, splitting front and back).
editor.knitOnly: I knit it in plain knit
editor.knitOnlyHint: “I knit it in plain knit” keeps the chart as drawn and shows plain knit stitches on the grid. The stitch count stays the same.

chartEditor.brokenSymbols: This pattern’s own symbols are damaged. Fix them in the project file.
chartEditor.help: Draw: tap or drag over cells. Select: drag to select a rectangle. Two fingers pan and zoom. Keyboard: arrows move the cursor, Shift+arrows select, Enter places the chosen symbol, Delete clears, 1–9 pick a palette symbol, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X and Ctrl+V copy, cut and paste, Ctrl+Z undoes.
chartEditor.whereNone: Tap a cell or use the arrow keys.
chartEditor.selectionHint: Choose “Select” and drag over cells. Without a selection, actions apply to the cell under the cursor.
chartEditor.heading: Chart editor: {{name}}

library.title: Symbol library
library.none: Nothing matches. You can add your own symbol.

symbol.inUse: A chart uses this symbol. Replace it first.
symbol.name: Name
symbol.nameHint: Give it a name, e.g. “bobble” or “k3tog”.
symbol.abbrHint: Up to 4 characters, e.g. B or 3t.
symbol.countsHint: How many stitches you take from the left needle and how many end up on the right one, e.g. k2tog takes 2, makes 1.
symbol.wsText: How to work it on the wrong side

patternEdit.title: Pattern: {{name}}
patternEdit.intro: A pattern is one grid to track: charts side by side in a round or row, e.g. the front and back of a sweater. Put the charts in the order of the pattern text, from the start of the round or row.
patternEdit.name: Pattern name
patternEdit.roundHint: Every round is on the right side; read the chart right to left.
patternEdit.flatHint: Rows alternate between the right and the wrong side. On the wrong side you read left to right and symbols swap meaning.
patternEdit.firstRow: The first row is on the
patternEdit.hasRows: I know the number of rows
patternEdit.openEnded: No row count: you knit e.g. “until the piece measures 30 cm”.
patternEdit.hasExpected: The pattern states the stitch count
patternEdit.expectedHint: We compare it with the sum of the segments to catch mistakes.
patternEdit.expectedOff: Turn on if the pattern says how many stitches should be on the needles.
patternEdit.layoutHint: E.g. “A.1 over 22 sts, A.2, A.3, marker, …”. A marker splits the round into parts such as front and back.
patternEdit.markerName: Name of the part from this marker
patternEdit.markerHint: E.g. Front or Back. Leave empty for a plain marker.
patternEdit.partialHint: The chart repeats horizontally and the last repeat may be partial.
patternEdit.startColumnHint: Cells counted from the left. You usually start on the right ({{w}}).
patternEdit.startRowHint: When this chart is shifted vertically against the others.
patternEdit.label: Label on the grid
patternEdit.addChart: Add a chart to the layout
patternEdit.previewEmpty: The preview appears once you add a chart.
patternEdit.previewHelp: Drag to pan. Pinch or use Ctrl and the mouse wheel to zoom.
patternEdit.trackStitches: Every stitch (tap stitches on the grid)
patternEdit.trackingHint: A row counter is enough for simple stitches such as ribbing or stockinette.
patternEdit.targetHint: With a gauge the app estimates the rows. You end the pattern yourself with “Finish pattern”.
patternEdit.continueHint: The chart starts with the row after the last one worked in that pattern, e.g. the front after the split continues A.2 of the body.
patternEdit.previewRowsOpen: Rows shown: {{shown}} — the pattern goes on repeating upwards.

diag.palette-reserved: {{chart}}: “.” is reserved for the cells of wide symbols.
diag.symbol-truncated: {{chart}}, row {{row}}: the symbol at cell {{col}} from the left needs {{width}} cells.
diag.orphan-continuation: {{chart}}, row {{row}}, cell {{col}} from the left: part of a symbol without its start.
diag.unknown-cell: {{chart}}, row {{row}}, cell {{col}} from the left: unknown character “{{char}}”.
diag.symbol-overflow: {{chart}}, row {{row}}: the symbol at cell {{col}} from the left runs past the chart edge.
diag.start-column: {{pattern}}: column {{column}} doesn’t exist in chart {{chart}} (it has {{width}}).
diag.stitch-count: {{pattern}}: the layout has {{actual}} stitches, the pattern says {{expected}}.
diag.empty-layout: {{pattern}}: the layout has no stitches yet. Add a chart.
diag.zone-cuts-symbol: {{zone}}: the repeat over {{stitches}} stitches cuts a symbol {{width}} cells wide (chart row {{row}}).
diag.ws-unsupported: {{zone}}: chart row {{row}} falls on the wrong side, and this symbol has no wrong-side instruction.
diag.chain-wrap: {{chart}}: the top row leaves {{produced}} stitches but row 1 needs {{consumed}}. The chart can't repeat vertically.
diag.chain-break: {{chart}}: row {{row}} leaves {{produced}} stitches but row {{nextRow}} needs {{consumed}}.
diag.flow-cable: {{chart}}, row {{row}}, cell {{col}} from the left: the cable starts on a different kind of stitch than the row below leaves. Check this cell.
diag.flow-texture: {{chart}}, row {{row}}, cell {{col}} from the left: knit/purl change (usually intended).
diag.size-list: {{label}}: {{actual}} values, but the project has {{expected}} sizes.
diag.legend-unknown-symbol: The legend refers to unknown symbol {{symbol}}.
diag.continue-unknown: {{placement}} in pattern “{{pattern}}” continues the chart rows of “{{source}}”, which has no fixed row count. The rows are fixed when you finish that pattern.
diag.continue-missing: {{placement}} in pattern “{{pattern}}” continues a chart that is not in “{{source}}”. Choose it again.
diag.continue-cycle: {{placement}} in pattern “{{pattern}}” continues itself through other patterns. Choose another starting point.
diag.size-index: The chosen size doesn’t exist. Choose a size in the project.

importer.title: New project from a PDF or picture
importer.intro: Choose a PDF with charts, or a photo or screenshot of a chart. We'll find the grids, symbols and legend, then check them together with you.
importer.limits: PDF, PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to {{mb}} MB and {{pages}} pages.
importer.privacy: The file is processed on this device only. Nothing is sent to the internet.

errors.wrong-type: This is not a PDF or an image (PNG, JPEG, WebP).
errors.too-many-pages: The PDF has too many pages. Choose a file with just the charts.
errors.too-many-pixels: The image is too large. Shrink it or crop it to the chart.
errors.unsupported: This browser can't open this image.

importer.straightenHint: Drag the four corners onto the corners of the chart, or tap a corner of the chart in the photo and the nearest handle moves there. For screenshots and scans choose “Don't straighten”.
importer.none: No chart found. Try a sharper photo, or build the chart in the editor.
importer.found_one: Found {{count}} chart. Check it against the original.
importer.found_other: Found {{count}} charts. Check them against the original.
importer.legendHint: Each legend symbol got a library symbol. Correct any that don't match and recognise again.
importer.symbolsHint: The file has no legend. Tick the symbols used in the charts: the fewer, the surer the result.
importer.chartsHint: The original is on the left, the recognised grid on the right. Cells outlined in red are uncertain: tap a cell to confirm or change it.
importer.nameHint: The name from the pattern, e.g. A.1.
importer.allChecked: Every cell was recognised with confidence.
importer.gridHelp: Tap a cell to select it. Arrow keys move the selection, Enter confirms, 1–9 pick a symbol, N goes to the next uncertain cell.
importer.descriptionHint: Sizes and the chart order of a round come from the pattern text. If it is in another file, load it or paste the text.
importer.sizesHint: Separate sizes with dashes, e.g. S - M - L.
importer.stillUncertain_one: {{count}} uncertain cell is left. You can fix it later in the chart editor.
importer.stillUncertain_other: {{count}} uncertain cells are left. You can fix them later in the chart editor.
importer.createInProject: Add the pattern to the project
importer.projectSizes: Project sizes: {{sizes}}. Numbers from the description for another number of sizes are left out.

position.hint: Enter where you are, e.g. after knitting without the app (shortcut: G)
position.title: Where are you?
position.intro: Enter the row you are on and how many of its stitches you have worked (from the start of the row). You can undo this.
position.introCounter: Enter how many rows you have finished. You can undo this.
position.stitchesHint_one: The row has {{count}} stitch to work.
position.stitchesHint_other: The row has {{count}} stitches to work.
position.previewRow: Last done: row {{row}}, stitch {{stitch}} ({{total}} in total).
position.previewRound: Last done: round {{row}}, stitch {{stitch}} ({{total}} in total).

finish.title: Finish pattern “{{name}}”?
finish.partial_one: Row {{row}} is started ({{count}} stitch) and will not count. If it is done, tap “{{button}}” first.
finish.partial_other: Row {{row}} is started ({{count}} stitches) and will not count. If it is done, tap “{{button}}” first.
finish.lastChartRows: Last chart rows worked — check them against the pattern, e.g. “end after an even row of A.2”:
finish.continueHint: Later patterns that continue the charts start with the next row. Finishing can be undone (“Reopen pattern”).
finish.partialRound_one: Round {{row}} is started ({{count}} stitch) and will not count. If it is done, tap “{{button}}” first.
finish.partialRound_other: Round {{row}} is started ({{count}} stitches) and will not count. If it is done, tap “{{button}}” first.

patternPanel.title: Pattern: {{name}}
patternPanel.phaseUnknown: Some charts continue an earlier pattern without a fixed row count. Their rows are fixed when you finish that pattern.
patternPanel.estimate_one: About {{done}} of {{target}} cm, about {{count}} row left.
patternPanel.estimate_other: About {{done}} of {{target}} cm, about {{count}} rows left.
patternPanel.noGauge: Enter a gauge in the project settings to estimate rows.

projectSettings.title: Project settings
projectSettings.name: Project name
projectSettings.patternGauge: The designer states {{stitches}} stitches and {{rows}} rows in 10 cm.

counter.thenNext: Finishes this part and goes on to: {{name}}.
counter.thenEnd: Finishes this part — the last one in the project.

project.name: Project name
project.export: Save the project to a file
project.patternsHint: You knit the patterns in order, e.g. ribbing, body, sleeves. Each pattern is one grid with charts side by side and its own progress.
project.noPatterns: The project has no patterns yet. Add the first one.
project.importPattern: Pattern from a PDF or picture
project.removeBody: The pattern, its charts and progress will be removed from this project.
project.patternNameHint: E.g. Body, Sleeve, Ribbing. If you leave it empty: {{name}}.

elements.recognised: Recognised from the words: {{words}}. If it's something else, change the kind.
elements.unsure: We couldn't tell the kind from the description — pick it from the list.
elements.pair: Made as a pair — you knit every part twice.
elements.unused_one: {{count}} chart belongs to no part and won't be in the project.
elements.unused_other: {{count}} charts belong to no part and won't be in the project.
elements.customParts: A custom project has no fixed parts: all charts go into one pattern. You can add more patterns to the project later.
elements.trackTitle: What do you want to track?
elements.trackHint: Click a part in the drawing or tick it in the list. The numbers are the knitting order of the pattern.
elements.orderUsual: Usual order ({{way}}) — the description doesn't give one.
elements.nameTitle: What will you call the project?
elements.nameHint: We suggest the file’s name. You can change it later too.
elements.sizesNone: We found no sizes in the description. If the pattern has several, type them below.
elements.sizesEditHint: Separate sizes with a dash or a comma, e.g. S - M - L.

preview.title: {{part}} — size {{size}}
preview.layoutSideBySide: {{charts}} — side by side (the description gives no arrangement)
preview.noCharts: This part has no chart — the project gives it a round counter. Assign a chart in “Correct” or add one later.
preview.cannotBuild: The grid can't be built from this. Check the charts and their arrangement in “Correct”.
preview.stitchesFrom: The stitch count follows from the charts' arrangement in the description and the chosen size.
preview.designerLead: Fix the pattern in the creator: the PDF charts lie on the grid as tiles you can move, widen and remove, and they wait in the library next to the ready-made pieces. The project will be created.
preview.designerLeadEmpty: Draw this part in the creator: the PDF charts wait in the library next to the ready-made pieces. The project will be created.

parts.title: Parts
parts.hint: Click a part to create its pattern or open it. The numbers are the usual knitting order ({{way}}).
parts.notReadyBody: These parts have no ✓ yet — open each and click “Done” when it is set up:

designer.title: Pattern creator: {{name}}
designer.sizeLead: Start with the grid: how many stitches a round or row has and how many rows this part has. You can change it later.
designer.widthHint: E.g. 226 stitches in a round of the body.
designer.heightHint: How many rows or rounds this part has.
designer.replaces: This pattern already has charts. The creator's grid will replace them.
designer.help: Click a cell to choose where a pattern starts or to paint a stitch. Two fingers or the mouse wheel pan and zoom.

hint.brush: Paint single stitches with the chosen symbol.
hint.eraser: The eraser removes stitches painted with the brush; the pattern underneath stays.
hint.tiles: Click a tile to select it (Shift + click: several) and drag it sideways to move it. Lay a library piece by clicking a column.

designer.brushHint: The symbol to paint single stitches with. The brush is always on top.
designer.libraryHint: Each pattern has its own size. Click a pattern, then a column on the grid: the tile stands on the bottom and repeats upwards.
designer.newPieceHint: Set the pattern's size and paint it. It is saved in the library and offered in every project.
designer.pieceHelp: Click or drag over cells to paint with the chosen symbol.
designer.offGrid: The start is outside the grid.
designer.onGridEmpty: Nothing placed yet — the whole grid is knit stitches.
designer.holdingHint: Set the width, then click a column on the grid — the tile stands on the bottom with its right edge in that column and repeats upwards.
designer.noTile: Pick a pattern from the library and lay it on the grid, or click a tile to change its width. Drag a tile sideways to move it.
designer.overlap: It doesn't fit here — the tile would cover “{{name}}”.
designer.layHere: Click to lay the tile from stitch {{col}}.
designer.fromFileHint: Charts from your PDF, for any part of the project.
designer.halfCut_one: The pattern crosses the side in round {{rows}}: a cable cut between front and back becomes knit stitches there. Move the tile or turn the split off.
designer.halfCut_other: The pattern crosses the side in {{count}} rounds ({{rows}}): cables cut between front and back become knit stitches there. Move the tile or turn the split off.
designer.pastingHint: Click a column on the grid: the tiles go from it to the left, as far apart as when copied.
designer.selectedManyHint: Drag one of them to move them all. Shift + click adds or removes a tile. Ctrl+C copies, Ctrl+X cuts, Delete removes.
designer.copied_one: {{count}} tile copied. Paste with the button or Ctrl+V.
designer.copied_other: {{count}} tiles copied. Paste with the button or Ctrl+V.
designer.cut_one: {{count}} tile cut. Paste with the button or Ctrl+V.
designer.cut_other: {{count}} tiles cut. Paste with the button or Ctrl+V.
designer.mirrorHint: Left of the axis shows the mirror image of the right side and changes with it; cables cross the other way. Double-clicking a line on the grid also turns a mirror on and off.
designer.mirrorOn: Mirror at {{line}}: left of the axis shows the right side mirrored.
designer.mirrorHere: Double-click the {{line}} line to mirror the right side onto the left.
designer.mirrorOffHere: Double-click the {{line}} line to turn the mirror off.
designer.mirrorConflict: This is a mirror image — lay the tile right of the axis.
designer.inMirror: This is a mirror image: change the pattern right of the axis.
designer.doneWithoutGrid: Done without a grid — just count rows
designer.lengthHint: The pattern repeats upwards to this length.

rows.label: Pattern length
rows.warnRounds_one: You have marked {{count}} round. Shortening the pattern to {{target}} rounds removes the marks above.
rows.warnRounds_other: You have marked {{count}} rounds. Shortening the pattern to {{target}} rounds removes the marks above.
rows.warnRows_one: You have marked {{count}} row. Shortening the pattern to {{target}} rows removes the marks above.
rows.warnRows_other: You have marked {{count}} rows. Shortening the pattern to {{target}} rows removes the marks above.

guides.label: Lines every ¼
guides.hint: Show or hide lines at ¼, ½ and ¾ of the grid width

layout.title: Layout and size
layout.hint: Click the charts in the order the pattern gives: the first starts at stitch 1 (on the right), each next one to the left of those before. Type over how many stitches each is worked.
layout.empty: No chart yet — the part will be counted in rows.
layout.cmNotInFile: The pattern gives no length for this part.
layout.noCharts: Add charts to see the grid.

fits.round: ✓ The charts fill the whole round.
fits.row: ✓ The charts fill the whole row.

over.round: The charts take {{used}} stitches, more than the round ({{count}}) — make them narrower or the round wider.
over.row: The charts take {{used}} stitches, more than the row ({{count}}) — make them narrower or the row wider.

layout.centred: Charts: {{used}} stitches, in the middle; {{rest}} knit stitches at the sides.
layout.centredHalves: Charts: {{used}} stitches, in the middle of the front and of the back; the rest is knit.

repeatTo.round: The pattern repeats upwards to {{cm}} cm.
repeatTo.row: The pattern repeats upwards to {{cm}} cm.
